problem_statement_fixed:
A RISC-V SoC needs a way to declare additional memory regions that must be protected by the PMP, beyond the standard read-only ROM region, with specific read/write/execute permissions. Regions declared this way must be automatically collected at link time and programmed into the PMP entries during PMP initialization, appearing as global entries (in the lower half of the PMP slots) shared between modes. After PMP initialization, the PMP registers must contain entries whose decoded start address, end address and permissions match the declared regions, and the declared regions must be retrievable as a set of structured entries.

For this purpose, the public header <zephyr/arch/riscv/pmp.h> must provide a macro PMP_SOC_REGION_DEFINE(name, start, end, perm). The macro must define a const entry of struct pmp_soc_region in an iterable section named pmp_soc_region. struct pmp_soc_region must have fields: const void *start; const void *end; uint8_t perm;. The start argument is the first address of the region and the end argument is the exclusive end address, so the programmed PMP entry covers [start, end - 1]. The perm argument may be a combination of PMP_R, PMP_W and PMP_X. The declared regions must be retrievable through the normal iterable-section interface on section pmp_soc_region, in the order in which PMP_SOC_REGION_DEFINE is used. The feature is available when CONFIG_RISCV_PMP is enabled, and the number of PMP slots is given by CONFIG_PMP_SLOTS; a global entry is in indices 0 through CONFIG_PMP_SLOTS / 2 - 1.
